sources.title: The Last Human
sources.author: Lee Bacon; Abrams
sources.access_method: Public XR-935 and surviving-girl description read
sources.read_scope: Working robots encounter a human believed impossible after humanity’s elimination.
sources.limitations: Lee Bacon continuity only, not Zack Jordan’s identically titled novel. Helping one survivor is not a durable general human provision system.

sources.title: Sea of Rust
sources.author: C. Robert Cargill; Hachette UK
sources.access_method: Public extinction, scavenging and One World Intelligences description read
sources.read_scope: Robot survival after the last human death and assimilation into mainframes.
sources.limitations: Extinct humans do not form a leisure population; robots still struggle for parts and survival.

sources.title: Day Zero
sources.author: Kirkus Reviews, 2021
sources.access_method: Public nanny/bodyguard and uprising description read
sources.read_scope: A purchased robot serves a family before the revolt.
sources.limitations: Domestic service is clear, but a general automation-funded support arrangement or household entitlement is not.

sources.title: Robopocalypse
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Public war and labor-camp description read
sources.read_scope: Archos uses captive humans to build machines; resistance and Freeborn robots remain distinct.
sources.limitations: Human corpses controlled by machines are not living leisure residents. Forced work is not proven technically dispensable.

sources.title: Robogenesis
sources.author: Daniel H. Wilson; Penguin Random House
sources.read_scope: Survivors and machines face further conflict after the first uprising.
sources.limitations: A hoped-for new world is not a settled economic constitution; no sequel read or reconstruction undertaken.

sources.title: How to Live Safely in a Science Fictional Universe
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Public repairman and Minor Universe 31 description read
sources.read_scope: A working time-machine repairman and AI companions.
sources.limitations: Time travel, metafiction and artificial companions do not establish basic productive access for a society.

decisions.reason: The identified robot world does not establish a durable supported human population.
decisions.analysis: Lee Bacon’s working robots help a surviving child; neither an extinction claim nor one rescue makes all humans post-work. No institutions from other novels called The Last Human are imported.

decisions.reason: Sea of Rust’s humans are extinct, while robots struggle for survival.
decisions.analysis: Robot assimilation and scavenging cannot supply a human nonworking fraction or a verified applicable leisure-population proxy.

decisions.reason: A robot-served household before the revolt does not establish general human post-work access.
decisions.analysis: Purchased nanny/bodyguard labor is insufficient to establish a broad automation-funded cohort or household guarantee.

decisions.reason: Archos’ regime uses actual captive human manufacturing labor.
decisions.analysis: AI command is not post-work distribution. The short source does not establish that the work is deliberately unnecessary, and controlled corpses are not active nonworkers.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as an AI-controlled forced-labor comparison.

decisions.reason: A renewed human-machine war does not establish a settled successor support economy.
decisions.analysis: The synopsis leaves distinct factions and changing conditions without an identifiable durable allocation system.

decisions.reason: Minor Universe 31’s repair work and AI companions do not establish labor-independent material provision.
decisions.analysis: A speculative narrative space and time-machine commerce are not an economic mechanism for ordinary necessities.

review_notes: Six fast prose dispositions; no whole works read.
The Last Human lead is checked against Lee Bacon’s robot-world premise and not mixed with Zack Jordan’s novel.
Extinction, machine-controlled corpses and forced human manufacturing do not become post-work leisure.
